description_good_justification: The README opens by saying what CRediT Matrix is: a web app that writes the contribution statement of a paper, with a heatmap and exports for journal systems. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/README.md
interact_justification: The README shows how to run it and links the package, element and plugins. CONTRIBUTING.md says how to report a bug or send a change. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/README.md
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the process: set up, run the checks, open a pull request, and what CI runs. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md sets the requirements: Conventional Commits, passing checks, tests for domain changes, translation keys, a changelog line and a sign-off on every commit. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
license_location_justification: The licence is in LICENSE at the repository root, and package.json names MIT. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/LICENSE
documentation_basics_justification: The README has a quick start, and the package, CLI, web element and plugins each have their own README. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/README.md
documentation_interface_justification: The package README documents the API and CLI, docs/element.md documents the web element, and a type snapshot test pins the public API. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/src/core/README.md https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/docs/element.md
sites_https_justification: The repository, the live site (with HSTS), npm and the Zenodo DOI are all served over HTTPS only. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/public/_headers
discussion_justification: Discussion happens in GitHub issues and pull requests: public, searchable, linkable, open to anyone with a free account. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/issues
english_justification: All docs, issues and pull requests are in English. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/README.md
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: commits land on main every few days, v0.8.0 and v0.8.1 were released in October 2026, and Renovate and Dependabot keep dependencies current. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/releases
repo_public_justification: The source is in a public Git repository on GitHub. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix
repo_track_justification: Git records every change with author and date, and each change lands through a pull request. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/commits/main
repo_interim_justification: Every change between releases is on main, not only the release commits. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged
version_unique_justification: Each release has its own version, and the release workflow refuses a tag that does not match the version in src/core/package.json. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/workflows/release-core.yml
version_semver_justification: The CHANGELOG says the project follows Semantic Versioning. It is still 0.x, and breaking changes are marked. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
version_tags_justification: Each release has a vX.Y.Z Git tag, and pushing that tag publishes the package. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/tags
release_notes_justification: CHANGELOG.md follows Keep a Changelog, and each GitHub release links to it. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No vulnerability in CRediT Matrix has had a CVE or similar ID. SECURITY.md says a fix will link its advisory from the CHANGELOG entry. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/SECURITY.md
report_process_justification: Bugs go in GitHub issues; CONTRIBUTING.md says what to include. A form exists for translation problems. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/issues
report_tracker_justification: GitHub issues track bugs and requests. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/issues
report_responses_justification: Every bug report gets an answer. So far only the maintainer and dependency bots have opened issues. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/issues?q=is%3Aissue
enhancement_responses_justification: Every enhancement request gets an answer. The roadmap says how to suggest one. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md
report_archive_justification: All issues and pull requests, open and closed, stay public and searchable on GitHub. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md says how to report a vulnerability, what to include, what is in scope and the timeline. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Reports go privately through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting, which is on for the repository. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have come in. SECURITY.md promises a reply within two weeks. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/SECURITY.md
build_justification: pnpm build builds the npm package and the static site, and CI builds both on every pull request. The census is a Python package built with uv. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
build_common_tools_justification: pnpm, Next.js, tsdown for the package, and uv for the census. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
build_floss_tools_justification: Every build tool is FLOSS: Node, pnpm, Next.js, tsdown, TypeScript, uv, ruff. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_justification: Public tests: Vitest unit and property tests, Playwright end-to-end and accessibility specs, JATS DTD validation, and pytest for the census. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/tree/main/src/core/__tests__ https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/tree/main/e2e https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/tree/main/census/tests
test_invocation_justification: pnpm test runs the unit tests, pnpm test:e2e the end-to-end suite, uv run pytest the census tests; pnpm verify runs what the pre-push hook runs. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_most_justification: Vitest enforces coverage thresholds (97% statements, 99% lines) on the TypeScript code, and Codecov tracks coverage on main. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/vitest.config.ts https://codecov.io/gh/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: Every pull request runs lint, typecheck, unit tests with coverage, JATS validation, the Playwright suite and the census checks. Main accepts a change only once the required checks pass. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md says a change to domain logic comes with tests, and the pull request template has a checklist line for it. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
tests_are_added_justification: Recent bug fixes came with tests, for example the XML entity fix (#138), the exported-names fix (#114) and the CLI error fix (#77). https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/pull/138 https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/pull/114 https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/pull/77
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md and the pull request template both ask for tests with a change. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
warnings_justification: Biome runs with its recommended rules plus the a11y, correctness, security and suspicious groups. TypeScript runs in strict mode. The census uses ruff and ty. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/biome.json
warnings_fixed_justification: pnpm verify runs lint and typecheck in the required Check job and the census job runs ruff and ty, so a warning cannot merge. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
warnings_strict_justification: Strict TypeScript, Biome's extra rule groups, and import restrictions that keep src/core free of React and Next.js. CI fails on any warning. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/tsconfig.json https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/biome.json
crypto_published_justification: The only cryptography is SHA-256 and RS256, both published standards, used through the browser's Web Crypto API to check ORCID's sign-in token. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/src/core/orcid-proof.ts
crypto_call_justification: The code calls Web Crypto (crypto.subtle) and implements no algorithm of its own. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/src/core/orcid-proof.ts
crypto_floss_justification: Web Crypto is built into every browser and Node, with no proprietary dependency. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/src/core/orcid-proof.ts
crypto_keylength_justification: The app generates no keys. It checks a signature against the RSA key ORCID publishes, and ORCID chooses the key length. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/src/core/orcid-proof.ts
crypto_working_justification: Only SHA-256 and RS256 are used, and the token header schema accepts only alg RS256. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/src/core/orcid-proof.ts
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No MD5, SHA-1 or alg none: the header check rejects any algorithm other than RS256. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/src/core/orcid-proof.ts
crypto_pfs_justification: The app does no key agreement of its own. The browser and the servers negotiate TLS. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/public/_headers
crypto_password_storage_justification: The app stores no passwords. It has no accounts (ADR 0002), and ORCID handles sign-in. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-no-accounts-or-server-side-storage.md
crypto_random_justification: The app generates no cryptographic keys or secret nonces of its own. The ORCID nonce is a SHA-256 of the reply, which binds the token to that reply. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/src/core/orcid-proof.ts
delivery_mitm_justification: The site, GitHub and npm are served over HTTPS only (the site sends HSTS). The npm package is published by GitHub Actions with npm provenance, and each file of the deployed site has a build provenance attestation. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/workflows/release-core.yml https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
delivery_unsigned_justification: No checksum is fetched over plain HTTP. npm serves the package integrity hash and its provenance over HTTPS. https://www.npmjs.com/package/credit-matrix
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No known vulnerability is open: Dependabot alerts and security updates are on and the alert list is empty. Recent advisories were fixed within days (#131, #141). https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/security/dependabot https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/pull/141
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Advisories are fixed first: #68, #131 and #141 each cleared a batch of Dependabot alerts. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/pull/141
no_leaked_credentials_justification: The repository holds no credentials. The ORCID client ID is public by design (the implicit flow has no secret). npm publishing uses trusted publishing with no token, and GitHub secret scanning with push protection is on. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/workflows/release-core.yml
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (default setup: JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, GitHub Actions) runs on pull requests and weekly. Biome, tsc, ruff and ty run in CI, and OpenSSF Scorecard runs weekly. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/security/code-scanning https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/workflows/scorecard.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's default queries cover injection and XSS, and Biome's security rules run on every change. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/security/code-scanning
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CodeQL has no open alert; the open code-scanning alerts are Scorecard findings about review and branch settings, none a vulnerability in the code. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/security/code-scanning
static_analysis_often_justification: It runs on every pull request, on main and weekly, and the lefthook hooks lint every commit. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
dynamic_analysis_justification: fast-check property tests feed random drafts through every format and random text to the importers. Playwright runs the built site under the production headers. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/src/core/__tests__/properties.test.ts
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The code is TypeScript and Python, which are memory-safe. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/README.md
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The tests run with assertions on, and the property tests assert round-trip invariants for every format. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/src/core/__tests__/round-trip.test.ts
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md asks for a failing property test's input to be added as a fixed test next to the fix. No known problem from dynamic analysis is open. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
dco_justification: Contributors sign off every commit under the Developer Certificate of Origin, and the dco workflow fails a fork pull request with an unsigned commit. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#sign-off-your-commits
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md says one maintainer decides, how proposals are weighed, and that a refusal gets a reason. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
code_of_conduct_justification: The project adopts the Contributor Covenant, with a way to report a breach. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md names the maintainer's role, who has access to the repository, npm and hosting, and what the bots do. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
bus_factor_justification: The bus factor is 1: the project has one maintainer, as GOVERNANCE.md and the assurance case say. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
documentation_roadmap_justification: docs/roadmap.md lists what is planned now, next and later, and what is not planned. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md
documentation_architecture_justification: docs/architecture.md describes the layers, the data flow and the calls that leave the browser, and ADRs record the design decisions. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/docs/architecture.md
documentation_security_justification: SECURITY.md's Security model section tells users what to expect and what to take care of: share links hold the draft, drafts in the browser are not encrypted, and which calls leave the browser. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/SECURITY.md
documentation_quick_start_justification: The README has a Quick start. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/README.md
documentation_current_justification: The docs change with the code: the pull request template asks for a changelog line, and the roadmap and README name the current release work. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md
documentation_achievements_justification: The README shows CI, Codecov, licence and Scorecard badges, but not this project's Best Practices badge yet; it is added once the badge is earned. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/README.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: End-to-end tests run axe over the main screens against WCAG 2.2 A and AA rules, Biome's a11y lint runs on every change, and docs/accessibility.md says what is and is not covered. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/docs/accessibility.md
internationalization_justification: The app has nine languages with ICU message catalogs, and a Playwright spec checks every catalog for missing keys and broken syntax. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/e2e/messages.spec.ts
sites_password_security_justification: The site stores no passwords. It has no accounts (ADR 0002). https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-no-accounts-or-server-side-storage.md
maintenance_or_update_justification: SECURITY.md says which versions get fixes (the latest release and the live site), and docs/deploy.md says how to roll back or roll forward a bad release. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/docs/deploy.md
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: SECURITY.md credits a reporter by name in the advisory and the CHANGELOG by default. No reports have come in yet. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md sets the process: a reply within two weeks, a fix or an agreed date within 90 days, then an advisory. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/SECURITY.md#disclosure-timeline
coding_standards_justification: Biome's config sets the style for TypeScript, ruff's for the census, DESIGN.md holds the UI rules, and CONTRIBUTING.md points to them. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/biome.json https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
coding_standards_enforced_justification: Biome runs in the required Check job and ruff in the required Census job, and lefthook formats staged files on commit. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
build_standard_variables_justification: Not a compiled C-style build: no CC or CFLAGS. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/package.json
build_preserve_debug_justification: No compiler options strip debug information; the package ships source maps and type declarations from tsdown. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/src/core/tsdown.config.ts
build_non_recursive_justification: Not a recursive make. pnpm build chains the package build, next build and a post-build script. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/package.json
build_repeatable_justification: Two builds of the npm package from the same commit give byte-identical tarballs (checked with npm pack twice and cmp, procedure in docs/deploy.md). The site's service worker build id is a digest of the built index page, not a clock or random value. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/docs/deploy.md https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/scripts/postbuild.mjs
installation_common_justification: The package installs with npm install credit-matrix (or pnpm), and the app runs from source with pnpm install and pnpm dev. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/src/core/README.md
installation_standard_variables_justific: No install step writes to system paths (DESTDIR). npm and pnpm install into node_modules. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/src/core/README.md
installation_development_quick_justifica: CONTRIBUTING.md has a Getting set up section: clone, pnpm install, pnpm dev. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
external_dependencies_justification: package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml list the JavaScript dependencies, census/pyproject.toml and census/uv.lock the Python ones. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/package.json https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/census/pyproject.toml
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot alerts and security updates are on, Renovate proposes updates monthly after a wait for new releases, and Scorecard checks known vulnerabilities weekly. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/renovate.json5
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Runtime dependencies come from npm and PyPI and are locked. The few vendored files each have a source and refresh path: role translations (scripts/fetch-credit-translations.mjs), fonts under the SIL OFL, and JATS DTD fixtures for tests. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/scripts/fetch-credit-translations.mjs
automated_integration_testing_justificat: The Playwright suite drives the built site under its production headers, the package test checks the published tarball's exports and CLI, and a Quarto test renders a real document. All run on every pull request. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
regression_tests_added50_justification: Every bug fix to code since 2026-04-25 came with a test (for example #138, #114, #110, #77, #65). The fix: commits without tests are dependency bumps, CI and deploy configuration, and a rename. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/commits/main
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Vitest fails below 97% statement coverage on the TypeScript code and Codecov tracks it on main. The Python census is not measured for coverage. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/vitest.config.ts https://codecov.io/gh/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md and the pull request template say tests come with a change to domain logic. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The app does not choose the algorithm: ORCID signs its tokens with RS256 and the app pins that. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/src/core/orcid-proof.ts
crypto_credential_agility_justification: No key or credential is stored. ORCID's public keys are fetched when a token is checked and matched by kid, so ORCID can rotate them without a release. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/src/core/orcid-proof.ts
crypto_used_network_justification: Every call that leaves the browser is HTTPS. The CSP connect-src names only HTTPS origins, and the site sends HSTS. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/public/_headers
crypto_tls12_justification: The app does not implement TLS. The browser and Cloudflare negotiate it. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/public/_headers
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: All calls use fetch, which checks the certificate. No code turns that off. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/src/core/upstream-fetch.ts
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: Lookups send only a public ORCID iD or DOI, over fetch; no private data is sent where a certificate check could be skipped. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/src/core/upstream-fetch.ts
signed_releases_justification: The npm package is published from GitHub Actions with npm provenance (a Sigstore-signed attestation naming the tarball), and SECURITY.md documents how to verify it: npm audit signatures, and npm view credit-matrix dist.attestations. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-a-release https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/workflows/release-core.yml
version_tags_signed_justification: Release tags (v0.8.1 and earlier) are lightweight tags, not signed. A ruleset lets only the owner create them. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/tags
input_validation_justification: Names, imports, share links, pasted statements, lookup replies and the ORCID token are checked with zod schemas and length limits before use, and property tests feed random input to the importers. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/src/core/import.ts https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
hardening_justification: The site sends a Content Security Policy with script hashes, Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy, Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy, Permissions-Policy, Referrer-Policy, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options and X-Frame-Options. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/public/_headers
assurance_case_justification: docs/assurance-case.md gives the threat model, trust boundaries, secure design principles, how common weaknesses (XSS, injection, forged ORCID proofs, supply chain) are countered, and the residual risk. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
osps_ac_02_01_justification: Only the owner can add a collaborator, by an invitation the person must accept. The owner is the only collaborator and no invitation is open. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
osps_ac_03_01_justification: The protect-main ruleset has a pull request rule, required status checks (Check, E2E and accessibility, Build, Census), linear history, and no force-push or deletion. Bypass is only through a pull request, so a direct push to main is refused. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/rules
osps_ac_03_02_justification: The same ruleset blocks deleting main and force-pushing to it. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/rules
osps_br_01_01_justification: No workflow runs on pull_request_target or workflow_run. Event data used in a run step goes through an environment variable first. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/workflows/dco.yml
osps_br_01_03_justification: Pull request code runs under the pull_request trigger, which gives fork pull requests no secrets and a read-only token. Cloudflare secrets sit in the preview and production environments, the preview job skips forks, and every checkout sets persist-credentials false. The release job that holds publishing rights runs on tag pushes only and runs no project code. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/workflows/release-core.yml
osps_br_03_01_justification: Every official channel is HTTPS only: the repository, the site (with HSTS), npm and the Zenodo DOI. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/public/_headers
osps_br_03_02_justification: The package goes out over HTTPS from npm with npm provenance, published by trusted publishing. The site is served over HTTPS. https://www.npmjs.com/package/credit-matrix/v/0.8.1
osps_br_07_01_justification: The .gitignore keeps .env files out, and GitHub secret scanning with push protection is on. CI uses OIDC where it can, so few secrets exist. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.gitignore
osps_do_01_01_justification: The README has a quick start, and the package, CLI, element and plugins have their own guides. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/README.md
osps_do_02_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md says how to report a bug and what to include, and sends vulnerabilities to SECURITY.md. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_02_01_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests are the public place to discuss changes and problems. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/issues
osps_gv_03_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to set up, check and open a pull request. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_le_02_01_justification: The source code is under the MIT licence, which is OSI-approved. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_02_02_justification: The npm package is MIT, and the bundled fonts are under the SIL Open Font License, which is OSI-approved. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/README.md#license
osps_le_03_01_justification: The licence is in LICENSE at the repository root. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_03_02_justification: The npm tarball holds LICENSE (the package's files list names it and the build copies it in), and the font licences sit beside the fonts. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/src/core/package.json
osps_qa_01_01_justification: The source is public at a fixed URL, and package.json, npm and the README all point to it. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix
osps_qa_01_02_justification: Git history on GitHub records every change with its author and date, and each pull request stays public. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/commits/main
osps_qa_02_01_justification: package.json lists the direct dependencies and pnpm-lock.yaml pins the full tree. The census has pyproject.toml and uv.lock. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/package.json https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/pnpm-lock.yaml
osps_qa_04_01_justification: It is one repository. The census lives in census/ in the same repository. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix
osps_qa_05_01_justification: The repository holds no generated executables. Build output (dist, out, .next) is in .gitignore. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.gitignore
osps_vm_02_01_justification: SECURITY.md names the security contact: GitHub's private vulnerability reporting, with a reply promised within two weeks. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_ac_04_01_justification: The repository's default workflow token is read-only, and every workflow sets permissions contents read at the top. Jobs that need more ask for it themselves. The CodSpeed workflow sets id-token write at the workflow level, wider than needed. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/workflows/codspeed.yml
osps_br_02_01_justification: Each release has a unique version, the release workflow refuses a tag that does not match src/core/package.json, and npm refuses a version used before. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/workflows/release-core.yml
osps_br_04_01_justification: CHANGELOG.md lists the changes of each version under Added, Changed, Fixed and so on, and each GitHub release links to it. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
osps_br_05_01_justification: CI installs with pnpm and uv from lockfiles (frozen-lockfile, locked), and both refuse very new releases. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/pnpm-workspace.yaml https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
osps_br_06_01_justification: The npm package carries a signed provenance attestation naming the tarball's digest, and SECURITY.md says how to verify it. Each deployed site file has a build attestation. GitHub releases attach no files. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-a-release https://registry.npmjs.org/-/npm/v1/attestations/credit-matrix@0.8.1
osps_do_06_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's Dependencies section says how a dependency is picked, how it is pinned, the cooldown on new releases and how Renovate updates them. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#dependencies
osps_do_07_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's Build from source section lists the prerequisites and the commands, and says what CI adds. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#build-from-source
osps_gv_01_01_justification: GOVERNANCE.md lists who has access: the maintainer for the repository, npm and Cloudflare, and the Renovate app. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
osps_gv_01_02_justification: GOVERNANCE.md describes the maintainer's role and the bots'. There is one maintainer, so there are few roles. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
osps_gv_03_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md has the requirements for a contribution: checks, tests, commit conventions, translations, sign-off. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_le_01_01_justification: A dco workflow checks the sign-off, but only on pull requests from forks, and it is not a required check. The maintainer's own commits are mostly not signed off. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/workflows/dco.yml
osps_qa_03_01_justification: The protect-main-checks ruleset requires Check, E2E and accessibility, Build and Census to pass, with a strict policy, before a pull request merges. Bypass is only through a pull request. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/rules
osps_qa_06_01_justification: CI runs the unit tests, the Playwright suite and the census tests on every pull request, before the merge. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
osps_sa_02_01_justification: The package README documents the API, the CLI and the formats, docs/element.md the web element, and the Quarto and MyST READMEs their plugins. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/src/core/README.md https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/docs/element.md
osps_sa_03_01_justification: docs/assurance-case.md is the security assessment: threat model, trust boundaries, weaknesses and their counters, and residual risk. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
osps_vm_01_01_justification: SECURITY.md has a coordinated disclosure policy with a timeline: a reply within two weeks, a fix or agreed date within 90 days. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/SECURITY.md#disclosure-timeline
osps_vm_03_01_justification: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is on, and SECURITY.md links the form. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/security/advisories/new
osps_vm_04_01_justification: SECURITY.md says a fix is followed by a published GitHub security advisory and a CVE request when the package is affected. No vulnerability has needed one yet. https://github.com/simonvanlierde/credit-matrix/blob/main/SECURITY.md#disclosure-timeline
